private.name: SambaNova Systems
private.rationale: Same sector (Chips & Semiconductors), same stage (Series A), post-money $11B

data.narrative:
SiPearl is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Philippe Notton that has raised €130M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 11 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors alongside three relevant public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD). The peer set includes later-stage private innovators such as SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient clustering within narrow cohorts. Only one true same-stage comparable and one adjacent-stage peer were identifiable, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for statistical reliability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material selection bias given the heterogeneity of capital requirements and commercialization timelines across semiconductor sub-segments. Public comps provide directional context but operate at vastly different scales and margin profiles, limiting precision for an early-stage private company.

The analysis therefore remains inconclusive on a specific valuation range without additional comparable transaction data or a clearer definition of SiPearl's technical differentiation relative to the identified peer set. Key uncertainties include the company's current run rate, technology maturity, and addressable market within semiconductor systems. A credible valuation would require either (i) expanded access to same-stage semiconductor fundraising outcomes, or (ii) a bottom-up framework anchored to unit economics and TAM assumptions specific to SiPearl's product roadmap.
